answer: Binding autonomous agent identities to optical physical unclonable functions forces Sybil attackers to absorb unamortizable hardware fabrication costs for each fraudulent node. To authenticate, a node routes coherent light through a waveguide trellis into a synthetic opal matrix on an etched terrace, recording the resulting speckle pattern. A primary limitation is that thermal fluctuations alter the optical speckle response, intermittently triggering false rejections of valid nodes.
